findings.description: SHEET-PUB-003 explicitly requires surfacing staleness 'via a best-effort in-tab banner and the TUI.' All three A-sketches trace this literally: each invents a `TuiNotifier` trait (`notify_stale` / `surface_staleness`) called unconditionally on failure, and each explicitly reasons the TUI call is NOT best-effort (only the banner is hedged) so it must never be swallowed — a real, spec-traced sub-decision. But the real code (lib.rs `Publisher`, testkit.rs, adapters.rs) has no TUI notification path of any kind: no trait, no callback, no push call anywhere. The only 'TUI surface' is the plain accumulated `stale: BTreeSet<String>` exposed via `Publisher::stale_tabs()` / `RepublishOutcome.stale_tabs`, which some component outside this scope presumably polls (per comments like 'the TUI is the fallback staleness surface' near write_stale_banner in lib.rs and in the republish.rs test `banner_write_failure_leaves_tui_as_staleness_surface`). All three B-runs independently confirm this same absence — none of B1/B2/B3 describe any TUI callback/notify mechanism; they only describe the tab remaining in the stale set. Both directions converge on the same unresolved gap: the EARS text asserts TUI surfacing as an active requirement, but the real code only operationalizes it as passive, unexercised state for an unseen consumer to poll.

The advisory write-lock protocol around `republish` is entirely code-invented and absent from SHEET-PUB-003's text, yet pinned unanimously by B1 (#7-8), B2, and B3 (#3): `republish` acquires the lock BEFORE any tab mutation; if `lock.acquire()` errs (held by another holder), republish writes to ZERO tabs, attempts no banner, and returns `published:false` with `stale_tabs` completely unchanged (see `HeldLock`/`republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing` in republish.rs and the `_guard = match lock.acquire()... Err(_) => return ...` branch in lib.rs). This is a distinct 'non-destructive refusal' code path, not a 'republish failure' in the SHEET-PUB-003 sense (no tab is added to stale_tabs). None of A1/A2/A3 anticipate any locking/concurrency concern — nothing in the EARS text hints at it.

The stale-banner's exact contract is fully pinned by tests/code but wholly unstated in the EARS: the literal text is `"STALE — last sync {ts}"` (em dash, 'last sync' verbatim) written to cell `'{tab}'!AA1` (adapters.rs `write_stale_banner`; republish.rs asserts `banner.contains("STALE")` and the timestamp). SHEET-PUB-003 says only 'a best-effort in-tab banner' — no wording, no cell. B1/B2/B3 all report the exact text; B2 and B3 additionally pin the `AA1` address.

Every Sheets-side failure mode — a failed `batch_update_view`, a failed `read_price_pass`, a failed `write_stale_banner`, a failed `set_tab_order`, and any step of the missing-tab bootstrap sequence (`ensure_sheet` → header `update_range` → retry data write) — collapses to the single `ViewError::PublishFailed` variant (lib.rs's `ViewError` enum; every `.map_err(|_| ViewError::PublishFailed)` in adapters.rs's `ViewSheetsAdapter`). SHEET-PUB-003 never discusses error taxonomy, nor that 'a republish' decomposes into a data write, an order reassert, and a banner write with different failure-visibility rules. Unanimous across B1/B2/B3 (B1 #1, B2 first Ubiquitous bullet + last boundary bullet, B3 #6).

`RepublishOutcome.published`'s exact truth table — true iff every tab's `batch_update_view` succeeded AND `set_tab_order` succeeded, while a `set_tab_order`-only failure is NOT added to `stale_tabs` (only per-tab data-write failures are) — is pinned in lib.rs's `republish` (`all_ok` flag) and confirmed by B1 (#9-10), B2, B3 (#7-8). SHEET-PUB-003 treats 'a republish' as one monolithic event with a single stale outcome; it has no concept of a `published` flag distinct from per-tab staleness.

Per-tab continuation — one tab's `batch_update_view` failure does not abort attempts on the remaining tabs in the same `republish` call (the `for tab in tabs` loop in lib.rs) — is confirmed unanimously by B1 (#5), B2, B3 (#1), but is a comparatively unsurprising engineering default rather than a sharp pin, so it is the weakest of the B-side findings.

notes: Read all five real files directly (lib.rs, testkit.rs, republish.rs, adapters.rs, adapters tests) rather than relying solely on the A/B summaries. The A-direction sketches are structurally near-identical (stale flag/state + reset-on-success + external-scheduler retry + best-effort-banner-swallowed + unconditional/reliable TUI call + log-unaffected-by-construction); the only internal wrinkle is A1 explicitly arguing for whole-view (not per-tab) granularity while A2/A3 model per-tab ViewState — none of the three actually model a multi-tab batch loop with independent per-tab continuation, consistent with them all missing that code-side behavior. The B-direction runs are unusually convergent, essentially re-deriving the same mechanics (lock protocol, banner text/cell, error collapsing, published truth table, per-tab independence, missing-tab bootstrap) with only minor variation in which exact bullet mentions the AA1 cell literal (B1 omits it, B2/B3 include it).
